# Droid Vault 2.0.0

The first stable release. This is the version where **debloat and restore finally
work as a pair** — you remove an app, and you can put it back, and the app will
tell you the truth about whether it did.

Everything below was found and fixed on a real phone, not in theory.

---

## If you only read one thing: what changed for you

### Debloat → Restore now actually round-trips

You debloated some apps, went to the Restore tab, and **the list was empty**.

The reason was that the Restore list was built from a list that debloat itself had
just emptied. Android keeps a short list of the apps you have removed, but a
"remove permanently" deletes an app from that list entirely — so the tab meant to
put things back could never mention the things you had just taken away.

Now the Restore tab works from **your backup folder**, which always knows what you
have, and it shows only apps that are actually not installed. One app debloated,
one app listed. Nothing else.

### A restore now tells you the truth

This is the one we most want you to know about, because the old behaviour was
actively misleading:

> **"Restore Complete! Successfully restored 1 app."** — on an app that was not
> installed.

Two separate problems fed it. Android's "unarchive" command prints **"Success"**
and exits with code 0 whether or not it installed anything, and the engine was
trusting that exit code. Separately, a reinstall can leave an app present but
**disabled** — installed, impossible to launch, and still counted as a success.

Restores now install the app from your own backup, switch it back on, and then
actually ask Android whether it worked before reporting success. If it didn't,
you get the reason instead of a false "Done".

### The permanent uninstall now asks first

The button that removes an app **without keeping its data** used to be the
default, needed no confirmation, and could not be undone by the app. Now:

- **Keep Data is on by default**, so the normal debloat is reversible.
- Turning it off raises a dialog that says plainly that the app's data is deleted
  and it can only be put back from a Droid Vault backup.

### Backups stop leaving system apps behind

A system app — Chrome, for example — could be ticked, drawn with a checkmark, and
still silently skipped, leaving the button greyed with "0 Selected". Two different
rules were deciding what you could see and what would be backed up. There is now
one rule.

**This one matters more than it looks**: system apps are exactly the ones a ROM
flash destroys, and they are the ones that were being skipped.

---

## Other fixes in this release

- **A finished backup could cancel the next one.** The engine's "stop" step ran at
  the end of *every* command, including successful ones, and left a cancel marker
  behind. The next command in the same run would pick it up and report "cancelled"
  for work it had never started. You saw this as an import that copied every byte
  successfully and then said **"Import cancelled"**.
- **Import now updates the list it just filled.** After importing, restored apps
  stayed missing from the list until you left the screen and came back — on the
  one screen that shows you what the import did.
- **Partition backups and flashing now join the queue.** Imaging a partition is
  the same engine as a backup and was the only operation that could run alongside
  one. A backup that ran out of time would kill a partition copy halfway through.
- **A slow check no longer looks like a broken one.** If the app could not finish
  verifying the engine within ten seconds, it reported your engine as *stale* when
  it was fine. It now says "Could not be checked".
- **Debloat's button no longer asks a question it cannot answer.** Adding a rule
  to an automation configuration with no labels defined showed an empty field and
  a dead button, with no explanation. It now tells you to create a label first.
- **Wi-Fi networks are no longer saved with the wrong security.** Some Wi-Fi
  networks were restored as *open* because the credential type wasn't recognised.
  Droid Vault now reads the format correctly and **skips** anything it cannot
  identify rather than downgrading it to an unprotected network.
- **Restore no longer reuses a phone's Android ID**, and restore permissions
  silently, unless you turn those on.
- **Debloated apps are relabelled for the app they belong to**, so a restored app
  opens instead of hiding its own data.
- Text and layout fixes across Settings, About and the progress dialogs.

---

## Before you upgrade

- **Keep your existing backup folder.** Nothing about your backups changes, and
  Droid Vault does not touch it on upgrade.
- **Read it in this folder, not the app's own storage.** The point of the backup
  folder is that it survives a reinstall or a flash. If you move it to a cloud
  drive, read it back into a new folder, and only then let the app import it.
- **Upgrading replaces the app.** Your preferences and scheduled jobs are kept;
  the backup folder and everything in it is untouched.

## Requirements

- A **rooted** device (Magisk, KernelSU or APatch)
- **Android 10 or newer**

## Choosing the right file

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `app-arm64-v8a-release.apk` | Most modern phones (2017 and newer) — this is almost certainly yours |
| `app-armeabi-v7a-release.apk` | Older 32-bit devices |

If you are not sure, install the 64-bit one. If your phone is from 2015 or
earlier, try the other.

## Please keep an independent backup

Droid Vault is built and tested by one person, on one phone, on one ROM. It is
not audited, and it is not a substitute for another backup. The app's own
recommended flow is: export to a file, move that file off the phone, and only
then trust it.
